I do not know yet. Assume hundreds, not thousands; if that is wrong, context compilation needs filtering earlier.

Slower to get the first expansion working

The host can be swapped later

payload.reason: A pure engine keeps the rules testable and lets the host change once the hosting question is really settled.

Anthropic and OpenAI both enforce output schemas
A backend is allowed but not required

pros: History, export and earlier versions come free
One user, so loading the whole graph is fine
Derive everything on read, in memory

payload.reason: One user and whole-graph loads make a snapshot plus log the cheapest model that still keeps history.

items.title: Two-phase reason-then-extract

The token log says when filtering becomes necessary, with numbers

payload.markdown:
# Brainstorm Tool PRD v0

Oct 24, 2026 · @Ravin Gupta

## Problem statement (root v2)

Build an AI-driven brainstorming tool for IT/software problems. The user states a problem; the AI proposes solution options; each chosen solution breaks into sub-problems, which the AI expands again. The result is an AND-OR graph: problems where one solution is picked, solutions where every sub-problem must be solved.

The AI expands nodes; the user controls every selection. No backend is required: the app runs in the browser, stores each graph as a document plus an event log, and calls LLM providers directly with the user's own API keys. A default provider applies, with per-stage overrides (expansion, classification, stale check).

Later the tool is open source, so others can attach their own models and task types (classify, describe, plan).

## Users and scope

MVP serves one person: the author, using it to brainstorm their own software problems and to learn the AI mechanics by building them. One user per graph; no accounts, sharing or sync.

Second audience, after MVP: engineers who run the open-source build themselves and plug in their own providers and task types. Nothing in MVP may block that, but nothing is built for it yet.

## Core model

The graph has three node types. A problem is answered by picking one child; a solution is complete only when every child problem is resolved; a clarification narrows the context without expanding the graph.

| Node type | Children | User action | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Problem (OR) | Solution options | Select one | Children of the selected solution become active |
| Solution (AND) | Sub-problems, all required | None | Complete when every sub-problem has a selected solution |
| Clarification (OR) | Answer options + free text | Answer one | Adds a constraint to context; no new nodes |

Selection semantics:

- Selections are the only stored state per problem. Enabled/disabled is derived: a node is enabled if reachable from the root through selected edges.
- The active area is a subtree, not a path, because every sub-problem under a selected solution is active at once.
- Generated nodes are immutable and versioned. Regenerating creates a sibling version; it never overwrites.
- Each expansion returns one of: clarify, solutions, subproblems, leaf. The same JSON contract serves all four, with items, a differentiating axis, a recommendation, a suggested next sub-problem, and any assumptions the model made instead of asking.

## Design constraints

Standing rules agreed before the session. They apply to every decision below.

1. Persist decisions, derive everything else. Selections are source of truth; visibility, the decision summary and the PRD are derived views.
2. Derived views carry a hash of their inputs. A changed hash means stale, never silently wrong.
3. Staleness has two tiers. Red: an ancestor selection or the root changed, so descendants are certainly stale. Yellow: a sibling decision or a comment changed, so possibly stale; a cheap LLM check resolves it on open. Mark eagerly, regenerate lazily.
4. Comments are global amendments to the root problem. Small ones append; ones that change a constraint become a proposed root rewrite the user approves, which creates a new root version and marks the whole tree red.
5. The decision summary that feeds every LLM call is rendered by code from the selected subtree, never by an LLM, so it cannot drift. The PRD is generated by an LLM on demand and cached on the context hash.
6. The LLM may ask instead of expand: if a missing fact would change the options, it emits a clarification node first.
7. Context compilation is deterministic. Same state in, same bytes out, or the hash-based staleness breaks.

## Decisions

Four decisions are selected. Each is the one child of its problem node that is active; the alternatives remain in the graph, disabled.

| Problem | Selected | Alternatives (disabled) | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Root: runtime host | Browser-only SPA: static site, IndexedDB, direct provider calls | Browser + optional thin server; desktop shell (Tauri/Electron) | Matches "no backend required" without an abstraction for a server that may never exist. Revisit a desktop shell before building a proxy if local models become real. |
| Storage model | Document per graph + append-only event log, in IndexedDB | Relational tables; pure event-sourced with replay | One user, UI loads the whole graph; derive-on-read in memory. Ported from the server-backed tree. |
| Expansion contract | Adapter per provider: native structured output where available, prompted JSON + schema validation as fallback | Model-agnostic prompted JSON only; two-phase reason-then-extract | The adapter boundary is needed for the provider registry anyway. Validate even enforced output: schema guarantees shape, not sense. |
| Context compilation | Full context, token count logged per call, hard ceiling; past the ceiling, swap the decision summary for an LLM condensation cached on hash | Relevance-filtered via embeddings | Hundreds of nodes fit easily. The token log says when filtering becomes necessary, with numbers. |

Context for every expansion call = root (current version) + comments + code-rendered decision summary of the active subtree + this node's ancestor chain.

## Assumptions

Facts the engine assumed instead of asking, or where the user answered "I don't know". Correcting any of these is a comment; it marks dependent nodes yellow.

| Assumption | Chosen default | If wrong |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Graph size | Hundreds of nodes per graph, not thousands | Context compilation needs relevance filtering earlier |
| Provider support | Anthropic or OpenAI; both enforce output schemas | Fallback path (prompted JSON) carries more load |
| No backend | Soft: not required, optional later | If hard, drop the "optional server" alternative entirely |
| Models | API keys only for MVP; local models (Ollama, LM Studio) later | Local models bring per-server CORS setup, or a desktop shell |
| Per-stage providers | One default provider, per-stage overrides | Manual per stage adds config burden; single model loses the cost lever |

## Open sub-problems

All four are required by the selected root solution and have no selection yet. Suggested order follows dependency.

| # | Sub-problem | Status | What it must settle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A.7 | Provider registry and key storage | TBD | Adapter interface, per-stage mapping, where keys live in the browser, per-provider browser-call quirks |
| A.4 | Staleness tracking | TBD | Dependency recording per node, red/yellow marking, the cheap on-open check, "restart from here" warning at the highest stale node |
| A.5 | Graph canvas UI | TBD | DAG layout, selected-subtree highlight, disabled dimming, stale marks, comment entry, assumption display |
| A.6 | PRD generation | TBD | Prompt over the decision summary, cache keyed on context hash, export |

A.7 comes first: A.4 needs a cheap model slot, and A.2 (decided) is implemented inside A.7's adapter.

## Non-goals for MVP

- Accounts, sharing, real-time collaboration, sync between devices
- A server of any kind, including a proxy for providers
- Local model support
- Node sharing across branches (same sub-problem under two solutions). Decisions port by hand via a ported\_from link; automatic merge waits until the identity rule (problem text + inherited constraints) is designed
- Per-node notes. Comments are global only
- Relevance filtering of context via embeddings

## Decision history

The graph holds two root versions. Version 1 and its subtree stay stored and disabled.

| Event | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Root v1 clarified: solo learning project, one user per graph, web app with canvas | Three answers recorded; the audience answer carried a comment about open source and pluggable models |
| Root v1 selected: server-backed web app (Node + Postgres) | Chosen against the engine's recommendation (engine library + thin host) |
| Storage, contract and context decided under v1 | Doc + event log in Postgres; provider-enforced schema; full context + summarize |
| Comment: storage is a document, so no backend is needed; multiple providers per stage | Marked all three decisions yellow; cheap check found it contradicts the root selection |
| Root rewritten to v2, approved with three defaults filled in by the engine | Whole tree red; root options regenerated as version 2 |
| Root v2 selected: browser-only SPA | Storage and context ported from v1; contract re-expanded and re-decided as adapter per provider |

## Repository structure

Decision added 2026-10-24: the engine and the web client are separate repositories. The engine is a published TypeScript package that owns every rule in this PRD; the client is a rendering system over it. The two specs below are the handover documents for Claude Code.

| Repo | Owns | Spec |
| --- | --- | --- |
| brainstorm-engine | Event log, reducer, selectors, context compiler, expansion contract, provider adapters, staleness, PRD generation | Brainstorm Engine Spec |
| brainstorm-web | React outline and canvas, IndexedDB adapter, settings and keys, deploy | Brainstorm Web Client Spec |

The engine never imports a UI or a database. The client never computes a graph fact. A feature the client needs and the engine lacks is an engine change first.

## Handover sequence for Claude Code

Run one milestone per session, engine before client, in this order. Give each session the PRD, the relevant spec, and its CLAUDE.md.

1. Engine E0, E1: contract and reducer, with the design-session fixture replaying green. Nothing else until this passes.
2. Client C0, C1: scaffold and a read-only outline rendering the same fixture. This proves the boundary.
3. Engine E2, E3: context compiler, providers, first real expand from a Node script.
4. Client C2, C3, C4: interactions, persistence, expand with a real key. The tool is now usable.
5. Engine E4, E5, E6: staleness, root rewrite and porting, PRD generation.
6. Client C5, C6: staleness UI and the PRD panel.
7. Engine E7, then client C7, C8: publish, canvas, deploy.

First instruction in every engine session: write or extend the fixture test before implementing. First instruction in every client session: render from the fixture before adding the interaction.

payload.markdown:
# Brainstorm Engine Spec

Oct 24, 2026 · @Ravin Gupta

## Purpose and boundary

The engine owns all state and all logic; clients only render it and forward user actions. It is a TypeScript package with no DOM, no React and no direct IndexedDB: storage and LLM providers reach it through adapter interfaces.

| In the engine | Out of the engine |
| --- | --- |
| Event log, reducer, graph model, versioning | Any UI framework, components, layout |
| Derived state: enabled set, stale marks, completeness, decision summary | IndexedDB implementation (client implements StorageAdapter) |
| Context compiler and hashing | Key management UI, settings screens |
| Expansion contract, validation, prompts | Rendering of PRD or export formatting |
| Provider adapter interface, MockProvider, AnthropicProvider, OpenAIProvider | Canvas layout |
| Staleness rules and the cheap stale check |  |
| PRD generation and cache |  |

Rules that keep the boundary honest:

- The engine runs under Node and Vitest with the in-memory storage adapter and MockProvider. Every feature is tested there first.
- Package name: brainstorm-engine (scope to be chosen). Published to npm with semver; the client pins a version. Local development links the two repos with pnpm link.
- Exports are typed. A client never reaches into internals; if it needs something, the engine grows an export.
- Provider HTTP calls use the global fetch, so adapters live in the engine and work in both Node and browser. The Anthropic adapter sets the browser-access header when configured.

## Domain model

A graph is one brainstorming session. It holds a versioned root, a set of nodes, and node versions; selections live on problem nodes. Everything else is derived.

| Entity | Fields | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Graph | id, createdAt, rootVersions\[\], comments\[\], nodes{}, nodeVersions{}, selections{}, answers{}, prdCache{} | The snapshot shape. Rebuilt from events or loaded whole |
| RootVersion | version, statement, createdAt, approvedFromCommentIds\[\] | v1 is the original statement; later versions are approved rewrites |
| Comment | id, text, createdAt, mergedIntoRootVersion? | Global amendments. mergedIntoRootVersion set when a rewrite absorbed it |
| Node | id, kind (problem, solution, clarification), parentVersionId, currentVersionId, portedFrom? | Identity across versions. parentVersionId is the version of the parent that generated it |
| NodeVersion | id, nodeId, version, title, summary, axisValue, pros\[\], cons\[\], contextHash, inputs, generatedBy, tokens, createdAt | Immutable. Regeneration appends a new version with the same nodeId |
| ExpansionInputs | rootVersion, ancestorSelectionIds\[\], decisionIds\[\], commentIds\[\], answerIds\[\] | Recorded at generation time; drives staleness |
| Selection | problemNodeId → solutionNodeId or null | The only mutable state per problem node |
| Answer | clarificationNodeId → itemId or freeText | Answers to clarification nodes |
| Expansion | parentVersionId → kind, itemNodeIds\[\], axis, recommendedId, reason, suggestedNextId, assumptions\[\] | What one expand call produced for one parent version |

Node kinds and what their children mean:

- A problem's children are solutions; one may be selected.
- A solution's children are sub-problems; all are required.
- A clarification's children are answer items; one is answered, or free text. Answering adds an Answer, no new nodes.

Ids are ULIDs. Hashes are SHA-256 hex of canonical JSON (sorted keys).

## Event log

The event log is the source of truth. The snapshot is a cache of folding the log. Every event carries id, graphId, seq (monotonic per graph), at (ISO time), and type plus payload.

| Event | Payload | Effect in the reducer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GraphCreated | graphId, statement | Root v1, empty graph |
| CommentAdded | commentId, text | Append comment; mark all enabled node versions yellow |
| RootRewritten | version, statement, mergedCommentIds\[\] | New root version; mark every node version red |
| NodeExpanded | parentVersionId, kind, items\[\] (new nodeIds + versions), axis, recommendedId, reason, suggestedNextId, assumptions\[\], contextHash, inputs, generatedBy, tokens | Create nodes and versions; record the Expansion |
| NodeRegenerated | nodeId, newVersion (same shape as one item), contextHash, inputs | Append a version; children of the old version stay attached to it |
| SolutionSelected | problemNodeId, solutionNodeId or null | Set selection; mark descendants of the old selection as disabled (derived), mark versions under the new path for re-check |
| ClarificationAnswered | clarificationNodeId, itemId or freeText | Set answer; mark enabled descendants of the clarification yellow |
| NodePorted | sourceNodeId, targetParentVersionId, newNodeId | Copy the node and its current version under a new parent with portedFrom set; copy its selection if it had one |
| StaleChecked | nodeVersionId, verdict (fresh, stale), reason, contextHash | Clear or confirm a yellow mark for that hash |
| PrdGenerated | contextHash, markdown, generatedBy, tokens | Cache entry; not a graph change |

Invariants the reducer enforces, and tests assert:

- seq is contiguous per graph; a gap or duplicate is rejected before folding.
- A SolutionSelected whose solutionNodeId is not a child of problemNodeId is rejected.
- A NodeVersion is never mutated after NodeExpanded or NodeRegenerated.
- RootRewritten increments version by exactly one.
- Folding the same log twice yields byte-identical canonical snapshots (determinism).

## Reducer and derived state

reduce(snapshot, event) → snapshot is a pure function. Derived views are computed from the snapshot by pure selectors and never stored in the log.

| Derived view | Definition | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| enabledSet | Node ids reachable from the root by following: root → every root-level problem; problem → its selected solution only; solution → all its sub-problems; clarification → nothing | Client dimming, context compiler, stale marking |
| activeSubtree | enabledSet restricted to the current root version's descendants | Decision summary |
| staleMarks | nodeVersionId → red, yellow, or none (see Staleness rules) | Client marks, regenerate prompts |
| completeness | Count of enabled problem nodes with no selection, plus enabled clarifications with no answer | Client progress, PRD readiness |
| decisionSummary | Deterministic text: root statement, comments in order, then one line per enabled problem with a selection: "\<problem title> → \<solution title>" in depth-first order | Context compiler, PRD prompt |
| ancestorChain(nodeId) | Titles from root to the node, with the selected solution at each problem level | Context compiler |
| suggestedNext | From the lowest expanded enabled solution with unresolved sub-problems, the suggestedNextId of its Expansion, else the first unresolved | Client "next" affordance |

Selectors are memoised by snapshot identity. A client renders from the snapshot and these selectors only.

## Context compiler and hashing

compileContext(snapshot, nodeId) returns the exact text sent to a provider plus the hash and the inputs record. It is deterministic: same snapshot and node in, same bytes out.

Sections, in order, each under a fixed heading:

1. Root problem: the current root version statement.
2. Comments: every comment not yet merged into the current root version, in seq order.
3. Decisions so far: the decisionSummary.
4. Answers so far: every answered clarification in the active subtree, as "Q → A".
5. This node: the ancestorChain, then the node's own title and summary.
6. Task: the kind-specific instruction (expand a problem into solutions, a solution into sub-problems, or decide whether to ask a clarification first).

Hashing: contextHash = sha256(canonical JSON of {rootVersion, commentIds, decisionIds, answerIds, ancestorSelectionIds, nodeVersionId}). The hash is over ids, not text, so a cosmetic prompt change does not mark the whole graph stale. A prompt template version is a separate field on NodeVersion.generatedBy.

Budget: count tokens with the provider's tokenizer when available, else characters divided by 4. Log the count on every call. Above a hard ceiling (default 24,000 tokens), replace section 3 with a cached LLM condensation keyed on the same hash; above a second ceiling (default 48,000), refuse with a clear error rather than truncating silently.

## Expansion contract

One Zod schema covers every expansion. The provider returns JSON matching it; the engine validates, then additionally checks sense (non-empty items, recommendedId present among items, axis set for solutions).

```typescript
const ExpansionOutput = z.object({
  kind: z.enum(["clarify", "solutions", "subproblems", "leaf"]),
  axis: z.string().optional(),            // required when kind = solutions
  items: z.array(z.object({
    id: z.string(),                       // provider-local, remapped to ULIDs
    title: z.string().max(80),
    summary: z.string().max(400),
    axisValue: z.string().optional(),
    pros: z.array(z.string()).max(4),
    cons: z.array(z.string()).max(4),
  })).min(0).max(6),
  recommendedId: z.string().optional(),
  reason: z.string().max(300).optional(),
  suggestedNextId: z.string().optional(), // only for subproblems
  assumptions: z.array(z.string()).max(5),
  leafReason: z.string().optional(),      // only for leaf
});
```

Kind rules:

| Parent kind | Allowed output kinds | Item meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| problem | clarify, solutions, leaf | clarify: answer options for one question; solutions: options differing on axis; leaf: actionable by one engineer in a few days, no expansion |
| solution | clarify, subproblems | subproblems: all required; suggestedNextId names the most constraining |
| clarification | none | Clarifications are never expanded |

Prompt requirements, enforced by eval fixtures rather than code: options must differ on the named axis, not be rewordings; cheapest or simplest option listed first; every made-up number labeled illustrative; ask (clarify) only when a missing fact would change the options.

## Provider adapter

A provider is anything that turns a compiled context into an ExpansionOutput or a text completion. The engine ships three; the client registers which to use per stage.

```typescript
interface Provider {
  id: string;                                   // "anthropic", "openai", "mock"
  capabilities: { structuredOutput: boolean; tokenizer: boolean };
  complete(req: {
    system: string; user: string;
    schema?: ZodSchema; maxTokens: number; model: string;
  }): Promise<{ text?: string; json?: unknown; tokens: { in: number; out: number } }>;
  countTokens?(text: string): Promise<number>;
}

type Stage = "expand" | "staleCheck" | "summarize" | "prd";
interface ProviderRegistry {
  default: { providerId: string; model: string };
  overrides: Partial<Record<Stage, { providerId: string; model: string }>>;
}
```

| Adapter | Enforcement | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MockProvider | Returns fixtures keyed by contextHash or by a scripted queue | Used by every engine test; never calls the network |
| AnthropicProvider | Tool-use with the Zod schema converted to JSON Schema | Sets the direct-browser-access header when options.browser is true |
| OpenAIProvider | Structured outputs (json\_schema) | Milestone 7; not needed for MVP |

Fallback path: when capabilities.structuredOutput is false, the engine appends the JSON schema to the prompt, parses the first JSON object in the reply, validates, and retries once with the validation error appended. Two failures surface as a typed EngineError, never a thrown string.

## Storage adapter

The engine defines the interface and ships an in-memory implementation. The web client implements it over IndexedDB. The engine never imports a database.

```typescript
interface StorageAdapter {
  listGraphs(): Promise<{ id: string; title: string; updatedAt: string }[]>;
  appendEvent(e: GraphEvent): Promise<void>;        // must reject on seq conflict
  readEvents(graphId: string, fromSeq?: number): Promise<GraphEvent[]>;
  readSnapshot(graphId: string): Promise<{ snapshot: Graph; seq: number } | null>;
  writeSnapshot(graphId: string, snapshot: Graph, seq: number): Promise<void>;
  deleteGraph(graphId: string): Promise<void>;
}
```

Load path: read the snapshot, then fold any events with seq above the snapshot's seq. Write path: append the event first, then update the snapshot. If the snapshot write fails, the next load repairs it from the log. The snapshot is a cache; the log is the truth.

## Staleness rules

A node version is stale when the context it was generated under no longer matches the current state. Marks are derived from ExpansionInputs against the snapshot; nothing is stored except StaleChecked results.

| Condition | Mark | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| inputs.rootVersion differs from current root version | Red | Regenerate (new version) or port |
| Any id in inputs.ancestorSelectionIds no longer matches the current selection at that ancestor | Red | Regenerate or port |
| inputs.decisionIds differs from current enabled decisions (sibling branches changed) | Yellow | Cheap check on open, then StaleChecked |
| inputs.commentIds misses a current comment, or inputs.answerIds misses a current answer in the active subtree | Yellow | Cheap check on open |
| A StaleChecked exists for this version with the current contextHash | Its verdict | fresh clears the mark; stale shows as red |

Rules:

- Only enabled node versions carry marks. Disabled branches are re-evaluated when they become enabled.
- The cheap check uses the staleCheck stage of the registry. Prompt: given the old context and the new context diff, are these items still valid options? Returns {verdict, reason}.
- The restart warning is computed, not stored: for the highest red node in the active subtree, count red descendants; the client shows "restart from here" when the count is 3 or more.
- Regeneration never deletes. The old version and any selections under it remain, attached to the old version id.

## PRD generation

generatePrd(snapshot) is on demand and cached. Input is the compiled context with a PRD task section instead of a node section; output is markdown. The cache key is the same contextHash scheme over the whole active subtree, so an unchanged graph returns the cached PRD without a call.

The prompt asks for these sections, in order: problem statement, users and scope, decisions with rationale, assumptions, open sub-problems marked TBD, non-goals, decision history. Unresolved problems are listed, never invented. The decision summary is passed verbatim and the prompt forbids contradicting it.

## Public API

The client sees one factory and the types. Commands are async because they may call a provider; dispatch is sync because it only folds an event.

```typescript
const session = await createSession({ storage, providers, registry, graphId? });

session.getSnapshot(): Graph;
session.subscribe((snapshot) => void): Unsubscribe;
session.select: {
  enabledSet(), staleMarks(), completeness(), decisionSummary(),
  ancestorChain(nodeId), suggestedNext(), restartWarning()
};

// user actions: fold an event, persist it
session.addComment(text): Promise<void>;
session.selectSolution(problemNodeId, solutionNodeId | null): Promise<void>;
session.answerClarification(nodeId, itemId | { freeText }): Promise<void>;
session.approveRootRewrite(statement, mergedCommentIds): Promise<void>;
session.portNode(sourceNodeId, targetParentVersionId): Promise<void>;

// provider-backed commands
session.expand(nodeId): Promise<Expansion>;
session.regenerate(nodeId): Promise<NodeVersion>;
session.proposeRootRewrite(): Promise<{ statement: string; mergedCommentIds: string[] }>;
session.checkStale(nodeVersionId): Promise<StaleVerdict>;
session.generatePrd(): Promise<{ markdown: string; cached: boolean }>;

// utilities
session.compileContext(nodeId): { text: string; hash: string; tokens: number };
session.exportEvents(): Promise<GraphEvent[]>;
```

Errors are typed EngineError values with a code (ValidationFailed, ProviderFailed, ContextTooLarge, SeqConflict, InvalidSelection). The client switches on code; it never parses messages.

## Test fixture: the design session

The session that produced this spec, replayed as an event log. Every NodeExpanded uses MockProvider fixtures, so the whole run is deterministic and needs no network. Ids are readable here; the fixture file uses them as given.

| seq | Event | Key payload |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | GraphCreated | statement: "AI-driven brainstorming tool for IT/software problems, AND-OR graph, user controls selection" |
| 2 | NodeExpanded | parent root-v1 → kind clarify, node Q1 (audience, collab, surface) |
| 3 | ClarificationAnswered | Q1 → solo, one user, web canvas; freeText "later open source, pluggable models and task types" |
| 4 | CommentAdded | c7: "Later open source; others attach own models for classify, describe, plan" |
| 5 | NodeExpanded | parent root-v1 → kind solutions, axis "where engine and state live", items A-server, B-local, C-library; recommended C |
| 6 | SolutionSelected | root → A-server |
| 7 | NodeExpanded | parent A-server → kind subproblems, items A1-storage … A7-api; suggestedNext A1 |
| 8 | NodeExpanded | parent A1 → solutions, items relational, doc+log, pure-events; recommended doc+log |
| 9 | SolutionSelected | A1 → doc+log |
| 10 | NodeExpanded | parent A2 → solutions; recommended provider-enforced |
| 11 | SolutionSelected | A2 → provider-enforced |
| 12 | NodeExpanded | parent A3 → solutions |
| 13 | SolutionSelected | A3 → full+summarize |
| 14 | CommentAdded | c8: "doc + event log means no backend; pure API, multiple providers per stage" |
| 15 | RootRewritten | version 2, mergedCommentIds \[c8\] |
| 16 | NodeExpanded | parent root-v2 → solutions, axis "runtime host", items A2-spa, B2-optional-server, C2-desktop; recommended A2-spa |
| 17 | SolutionSelected | root → A2-spa |
| 18 | NodePorted | A1 → under A2-spa as A1p (selection doc+log copied) |
| 19 | NodePorted | A3 → under A2-spa as A3p |
| 20 | NodeExpanded | parent A2p-contract (new under A2-spa) → solutions; recommended adapter-per-provider |
| 21 | SolutionSelected | A2p → adapter-per-provider |

Expected state after seq 21, asserted by the test:

- Root version is 2; comment c8 has mergedIntoRootVersion 2; c7 is unmerged and appears in compiled context.
- enabledSet contains A2-spa, A1p, A3p, A2p and their selected children; it excludes A-server and everything under it.
- Every version generated under root v1 that is still enabled is red; after seq 17 none are enabled, so staleMarks has no red entries. A1p and A3p carry the portedFrom link and inherit no mark.
- completeness reports 4 unresolved problems under A2-spa (staleness, canvas UI, PRD generation, provider registry).
- decisionSummary lists exactly: root → Browser-only SPA; storage → doc + event log; context → full + summarize; contract → adapter per provider.
- Folding seq 1–21 twice gives byte-identical canonical snapshots.
- Checkpoint after seq 14: A1, A2, A3 versions are yellow; after seq 15 they are red; after seq 17 they are disabled and unmarked.

Additional fixtures to add as they are found: a comment that appends without a rewrite (yellow only, cheap check returns fresh), a regenerate that leaves a selection on the old version, a rejected SolutionSelected with a non-child id.

## Milestones

One milestone per Claude Code session. Each ends green under Vitest with MockProvider and the in-memory adapter; no milestone needs an API key until E3.

| # | Milestone | Done when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E0 | Contract as code | Zod schemas for Graph, GraphEvent, NodeVersion, ExpansionOutput, EngineError; package builds to ESM + types; no runtime code yet |
| E1 | Reducer, selectors, fixture | reduce() and all selectors implemented; the design-session fixture replays and every assertion in that section passes; determinism test passes |
| E2 | Context compiler | compileContext() produces the six sections; hash is stable across runs; token counting with fallback; ceilings enforced with typed errors |
| E3 | Providers and expand | Provider interface, MockProvider, AnthropicProvider (browser header option); session.expand() and regenerate() run end to end from a Node script against the real API once, then against mocks in CI |
| E4 | Staleness | staleMarks selector matches the rules table; checkStale() via the staleCheck stage; restartWarning(); fixture checkpoints at seq 14, 15, 17 pass |
| E5 | Root rewrite and porting | proposeRootRewrite() returns a merged statement; approveRootRewrite() and portNode() fold correctly; fixture seq 15–19 covered |
| E6 | PRD generation | generatePrd() with cache keyed on hash; cached flag correct; prompt forbids contradicting the decision summary |
| E7 | Publish | npm publish with semver 0.1.0; README covers createSession, adapters, and how to implement StorageAdapter; OpenAIProvider added |

Order matters: E1 before E2 so the hash has real inputs; E4 after E3 so the cheap check has a provider; E7 last so the client never pins a moving target during development (use pnpm link until then).

## CLAUDE.md for the engine repo

Copy this into the repo root as CLAUDE.md.

```markdown
# brainstorm-engine

Pure TypeScript engine for an AND-OR brainstorming graph. No DOM, no React, no database imports.

## Non-negotiables
- Event log is the source of truth. The snapshot is a cache. Never mutate a NodeVersion.
- reduce() and every selector are pure and deterministic. If a test is flaky, the bug is here.
- Storage and LLM providers go through adapters. Ship in-memory + MockProvider; real adapters use global fetch only.
- Every feature lands with a Vitest test that runs under MockProvider. No test hits the network.
- Errors are typed EngineError with a code. Never throw strings.

## Layout
- src/schema/     Zod schemas and types (E0)
- src/reducer/    reduce(), invariants
- src/select/     memoised selectors (enabledSet, staleMarks, decisionSummary, ...)
- src/context/    compileContext(), hashing, token budget
- src/providers/  Provider interface, mock, anthropic, openai
- src/storage/    StorageAdapter interface, memory adapter
- src/session/    createSession() and commands
- test/fixtures/  design-session.events.json + expected snapshots

## Working rules
- Start each milestone by writing or extending the fixture test, then implement until green.
- Do not add a feature the spec does not name. Propose it in a comment on the spec instead.
- Keep public API changes in CHANGELOG.md; the web client pins versions.

## Commands
- pnpm test        Vitest
- pnpm build       tsup to dist/ (ESM + d.ts)
- pnpm link --global   for local development with the web client
```

# Brainstorm Web Client Spec

Oct 24, 2026 · @Ravin Gupta

## Purpose

The web client renders an engine snapshot and forwards user actions to the engine session. It holds no business logic: no graph walking, no staleness math, no prompt text, no provider calls of its own.

The test of the boundary: if a behaviour could be wrong, the fix belongs in brainstorm-engine. If only the pixels could be wrong, it belongs here. When the client needs a value the engine does not expose, the engine grows a selector; the client never recomputes it.

## Stack and repo setup

| Concern | Choice | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build | Vite + React 18 + TypeScript | Static output, fast dev loop |
| Engine dependency | brainstorm-engine from npm, pinned exact version; pnpm link during development | Client never vendors engine code |
| Persistence | Dexie over IndexedDB, implementing the engine's StorageAdapter | Engine defines the interface |
| State in React | useSyncExternalStore over session.subscribe | Snapshot is the single store; no Redux or Zustand |
| Styling | Tailwind | Fast; no design system yet |
| Tree view | Custom collapsible outline (milestone C1) | 80% of the UX, 10% of the effort |
| Canvas | React Flow + elkjs layout (milestone C7) | Only after the outline proves the engine |
| Tests | Vitest + Testing Library; engine always MockProvider | No network in tests |
| Hosting | Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages | Static; no server |

Two repos:

- brainstorm-engine: the package. Changes there are released with a version bump.
- brainstorm-web: this client. Depends on the published package; during development, pnpm link --global brainstorm-engine in the client after pnpm link --global in the engine.

Upgrading the engine is a one-line version bump plus a CHANGELOG read. If the client needs a feature, the request goes to the engine repo first.

## State flow

One engine session per open graph. The snapshot is the only application state; UI-only state (which nodes are collapsed, which panel is open) lives in component state or the URL and is never persisted by the engine.

1. App start: build DexieStorageAdapter, read provider settings from localStorage, build the ProviderRegistry, call createSession.
2. Render: components read the snapshot and selectors through useSyncExternalStore. No component derives graph facts on its own.
3. User action: a component calls one session command (selectSolution, addComment, expand, ...). It shows a pending state on that node while the promise is open.
4. Engine folds the event, persists it, notifies subscribers; React re-renders from the new snapshot.
5. Provider-backed commands may take seconds. The node shows a spinner; the rest of the tree stays interactive. Only one expand per node at a time; the button is disabled while pending.
6. Errors arrive as EngineError codes. The client maps each code to a message and a recovery action (retry, open settings, shorten context) and never shows raw messages.

What the client never does: compute enabled or stale state, build prompt text, call fetch to a provider, mutate the snapshot, or write to IndexedDB outside the adapter.

## Screens and components

Three screens; the outline screen is the product for the first six milestones.

| Screen | Contents | Session calls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Graph list | Cards from storage.listGraphs(); new graph form (statement textarea); import events JSON | createSession per selected graph |
| Outline | Header: root statement (current version), version badge, comments panel toggle, PRD button, settings. Body: collapsible tree from the root, one row per node. Right rail: comments panel, assumptions list, restart warning | All user actions and expand/regenerate |
| Settings | Provider keys, default model, per-stage overrides, token ceiling display, export/import | None; writes localStorage and rebuilds the registry |

Outline components:

- NodeRow: title, kind icon, summary on expand, marks (see rendering rules), action buttons by kind. Problem rows show their solution children as a radio group. Solution rows list sub-problems with a "next" chip on suggestedNext. Clarification rows show answer options plus a free-text field, and an answered state.
- ExpandButton: on an unexpanded enabled node. Pending spinner while the promise is open. On a stale node the label reads Regenerate.
- OptionCard: for a solution item: title, axisValue, pros, cons, recommended badge with the reason on hover. Options are listed in the order the engine returns.
- CommentsPanel: ordered comment list, add box, and a Propose rewrite button that calls proposeRootRewrite and shows the merged statement with approve, edit, reject.
- AssumptionsList: every assumptions\[\] entry from enabled expansions, each with a Correct action that opens the comment box prefilled with the assumption text.
- RestartWarning: shown when restartWarning() returns a node; names the node and the count of red descendants, with Regenerate from here.
- PrdPanel: calls generatePrd, renders markdown, shows the cached flag, offers Copy and Download .md.

Keyboard: arrow keys move between rows, Enter expands or selects, c focuses the comment box. The pace is the user's; nothing expands automatically.

## Node rendering rules

Every visual state comes from a selector. The client reads the value and applies a style; it never decides the value.

| Selector value | Rendering |
| --- | --- |
| In enabledSet, selected (solution chosen under its parent problem) | Full opacity, bold title, radio checked |
| In enabledSet, not selected | Full opacity, radio unchecked |
| Not in enabledSet | 40% opacity, collapsed by default, radio disabled, no action buttons |
| staleMarks = red | Red left border; Expand button reads Regenerate; tooltip gives the reason (root changed, ancestor changed) |
| staleMarks = yellow | Amber left border; a Check button runs checkStale; result clears the border or turns it red |
| portedFrom set | Small link icon; tooltip names the source node and its old parent |
| Clarification answered | Options collapsed to the chosen answer with an Edit action |
| Expansion has assumptions | Note icon on the parent row; count badge; click opens AssumptionsList scrolled to those entries |
| Node has multiple versions | Version chip; click shows older versions read-only, with any selections made under them |

Old versions are never hidden and never editable. A selection that lives under an old version stays visible there, dimmed, so the user can see what regeneration orphaned.

## Persistence

DexieStorageAdapter implements the engine's StorageAdapter. Two tables, both keyed to allow the engine's load path (snapshot, then events above its seq).

| Table | Key | Indexes | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| events | \[graphId+seq\] | graphId | One row per GraphEvent, as emitted |
| snapshots | graphId | updatedAt | { snapshot, seq, title, updatedAt } |

Rules:

- appendEvent writes inside a transaction and rejects with SeqConflict if \[graphId+seq\] exists.
- writeSnapshot is best effort; a failure is logged, not surfaced, because the next load repairs from events.
- Export is the event array as JSON; import appends events to a new graphId. This is also how a bug report is filed: attach the export.
- Provider keys are not in IndexedDB; see the next section.
- Clearing site data loses everything. The graph list screen shows this once as a notice, with the Export action beside it.

## Provider keys and settings

Keys live in localStorage under one JSON object and are sent only to the provider they belong to, by the engine's adapter. The client never logs, exports or displays a key after entry.

| Setting | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic key | empty | Required for expand until another provider is configured |
| Default provider and model | anthropic, a current mid-tier model | Used for every stage without an override |
| Per-stage override | staleCheck → cheapest available model | expand, summarize and prd use the default unless set |
| Token ceiling display | from the engine | Read-only; shows the last call's count against the ceiling |

Browser-call quirks are the adapter's job, but the settings screen explains them in one line each: Anthropic needs the direct-browser-access header (the adapter sets it); OpenAI keys in a browser are at the user's own risk; local models are out of scope for MVP.

## Milestones

One milestone per Claude Code session. Each client milestone names the engine milestone it needs; do not start a client milestone before its engine dependency is green and linked.

| # | Milestone | Needs | Done when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C0 | Scaffold | E0 | Vite app builds; engine linked via pnpm link; types import; Tailwind and Vitest configured |
| C1 | Read-only outline | E1 | Loads the design-session fixture through an in-memory adapter and renders the tree with enabled/disabled styling; no actions yet |
| C2 | Interactions | E1 | Select solution, add comment, answer clarification; pending states; keyboard navigation |
| C3 | Persistence | E1 | DexieStorageAdapter passes the engine's adapter contract test; graph list screen; export/import |
| C4 | Expand with a real provider | E3 | Settings screen with key entry; Expand and Regenerate buttons; OptionCard with recommended badge; AssumptionsList with Correct action |
| C5 | Staleness UI | E4, E5 | Red and amber borders, Check button, RestartWarning, propose-rewrite flow with approve/edit/reject, port action on red nodes |
| C6 | PRD panel | E6 | Generate, cached flag, copy, download .md |
| C7 | Canvas | E7 | React Flow view beside the outline; elkjs layout; same selectors drive both views; selection sync between them |
| C8 | Deploy | E7 | Static build on Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages; README with setup and key instructions |

C1 is the proof that the boundary holds: a full tree rendered from a replayed fixture, with zero logic in the client.

## CLAUDE.md for the client repo

Copy this into the repo root as CLAUDE.md.

```markdown
# brainstorm-web

React + Vite client for brainstorm-engine. This repo renders engine state and forwards user actions. It contains no graph logic.

## Non-negotiables
- All graph facts come from the engine snapshot and selectors. Never recompute enabled, stale, completeness or ordering here.
- Never call an LLM provider from this repo. Never build prompt text here.
- IndexedDB is touched only inside src/storage/DexieStorageAdapter.ts.
- If a feature needs something the engine does not expose, stop and write the request as an issue for brainstorm-engine. Do not work around it.
- Tests use the engine's MockProvider and in-memory adapter, plus the design-session fixture. No network.

## Layout
- src/app/          routes, providers, session bootstrap
- src/storage/      DexieStorageAdapter + contract test
- src/settings/     keys, registry, localStorage
- src/outline/      NodeRow, OptionCard, ExpandButton, CommentsPanel, AssumptionsList, RestartWarning
- src/prd/          PrdPanel
- src/canvas/       React Flow view (C7)
- src/hooks/        useSession, useSnapshot, useSelector

## Working rules
- Start each milestone by rendering the fixture, then add the interaction, then the test.
- Pending state per node, never a global spinner.
- Map every EngineError code to a message and a recovery action in src/app/errors.ts.

## Commands
- pnpm dev / pnpm build / pnpm test
- pnpm link --global brainstorm-engine   (after pnpm link --global in the engine repo)
```
